title: kith-jmap: JMAP request body parsing
description:
Parse POST /jmap/api body and validate the JMAP request envelope.

What: Implement the HTTP handler and parse function that accepts a JMAP request, validates the 'using' capability array, and returns a parsed JmapRequest ready for dispatch.

Algorithm:
1. Define pub fn parse_request(body: serde_json::Value) -> Result<JmapRequest, JmapError>
2. Deserialize Value to JmapRequest using serde_json::from_value; on error return JmapError { type: 'invalidArguments', description: error message }
3. If using array is empty, return JmapError { type: 'unknownCapability', description: 'using array must not be empty' }
4. For each URI in using: if not one of ['urn:ietf:params:jmap:core', 'urn:kith:chat:1'], return JmapError { type: 'unknownCapability', description: format!("Unsupported capability: {uri}") }
5. If 'urn:kith:chat:1' is not in using, return JmapError { type: 'unknownCapability', description: 'urn:kith:chat:1 is required' }
6. Return Ok(parsed_request)
7. Expose as pub fn parse_request in kith-jmap lib.rs

Defensive programming rules:
- Never unwrap() — every path returns typed Result
- Validate using array BEFORE looking at methodCalls
- Unknown capability rejects the whole request (request-level error, not per-method)
- Cap method_calls at 16 entries; if exceeded return JmapError { type: 'requestTooLarge', description: 'maxCallsInRequest is 16' }
- No key material involved
- Input is untrusted (from network)

Tests:
- Valid request with known capabilities → Ok(JmapRequest)
- Empty using array → Err with type unknownCapability
- Unknown capability URI → Err with type unknownCapability
- Missing urn:kith:chat:1 → Err with type unknownCapability
- More than 16 method calls → Err with type requestTooLarge
- Malformed JSON object → Err with type invalidArguments
Oracle: Manually constructed request objects from RFC 8620 §3, not derived from code under test.
